evidence: coop/crates/coop-launcher/src/session.rs:2263-2273 can observe the server Ready event during checkpoint and set ready_seen=true while the checkpoint continues.

coop/crates/coop-launcher/src/session.rs:2308-2335 then calls establish_realtime_cutover with ready_seen=true, but its biased select drains every immediately available control event before the ready branch can activate interactions.

coop/crates/coop-launcher/src/session.rs:2357-2359 routes each drained interaction through RealtimeCoordinator::interact, and realtime.rs:169-175 intentionally discards it while interaction_ready remains false; the regression at session.rs:4599-4635 emits its post-Ready interaction only after checkpoint completion and therefore does not cover this interval.
findings.impact: An interaction produced after the launcher has observed server Ready but before an overlapping checkpoint completes is deterministically discarded as pre-Ready. This over-corrects F-58EDE2B0 and violates the sealed requirement to preserve post-Ready interaction FIFO; a user action during a slow checkpoint can disappear without an error.
findings.observation: The corrected checkpoint cutover has no boundary marker between interactions queued before and after Ready, so its drain-to-empty policy drops both classes.
findings.recommendation: Establish an explicit ordered interaction cutover at the instant Ready is observed. During checkpoint, consume and drop interactions only until that marker, then buffer post-marker interactions in FIFO order and submit them after checkpoint reconciliation. Add a synchronized regression that emits one interaction before Ready and one immediately after Ready while the checkpoint is still pending.

evidence: coop/crates/coop-launcher/src/realtime.rs:189-195 checks JoinHandle::is_finished only once before entering the select.

coop/crates/coop-launcher/src/realtime.rs:196-209 polls the JoinHandle first, but if that poll returns Pending and the driver completes before the already-buffered owner event is polled, the owner event can still win and be returned as lifecycle input without a second terminal check.

coop/crates/coop-launcher/src/realtime.rs:723-785 waits until is_finished is already true before calling next_event, so the new regression proves only the pre-select case and cannot exercise completion between the JoinHandle poll and owner-event return.
findings.impact: A peer close, transport failure, or owner-backpressure completion racing a queued lifecycle event can still let one stale peer event reach the ROM after the core has become terminal. Thus F-BDD4C8DE is narrowed but not fully resolved.
findings.observation: Task completion has polling priority, but terminal state is not rechecked after receiving a buffered owner event, leaving a poll-to-return race.
findings.recommendation: After receiving an owner event, recheck or nonblocking-poll the JoinHandle before mapping or returning that event; if the task finished, join it and return Terminal instead. Add a barrier-controlled test that makes the driver finish after its JoinHandle was first polled Pending but before a queued event would be returned.

evidence: coop/crates/coop-launcher/src/session.rs:3534-3550 can now return a successful grant, but every successful grant is immediately ready; the fake has no delayed mint seam for publishing a fresher PlayerState while mint is pending.

coop/crates/coop-launcher/src/session.rs:4441-4565 exercises a basic successful Ready/lifecycle path and session.rs:4572-4717 exercises one checkpoint cutover, but neither changes the coalesced state during mint nor induces active reset, lifecycle/interaction backpressure, or child failure.

The sealed LRA2-006 criterion explicitly requires deterministic coverage of freshest-state handoff, races, lifecycle backpressure, cleanup order, and task termination, while the focused filters pass without those active-session failure paths.
findings.impact: F-2D10E061 is only partially resolved: the happy path is now executable, but several required fence and teardown paths can regress without a failing activation-level test.
findings.observation: The corrected suite adds successful realtime integration but still does not execute freshest-state handoff during mint or active reset/backpressure/child-failure cleanup through the production lifecycle.
findings.recommendation: Add deterministic activation-level tests with a controllably pending successful mint, a later same-generation state, active reset, bounded interaction/lifecycle overflow, and child exit. Assert the freshest initial WebSocket state, zero post-terminal ROM output, one attempt, disabled lifecycle, joined coordinator/pumps/children, and cleanup ordering.
